questions.stem: Which situation best illustrates distributed computing?

options.why: That is data compression.

options.text: One laptop running a word processor
options.why: That is a single device.

options.text: A program running one instruction at a time
options.why: That is sequential computing.

questions.stem: What is bandwidth?

A robot is on a 6-by-6 grid of squares. Rows are numbered 1 to 6 from top to bottom and columns 1 to 6 from left to right. The robot starts in row 5, column 5, facing right. `MOVE_FORWARD()` moves it one square in the direction it faces; `ROTATE_LEFT()` and `ROTATE_RIGHT()` turn it 90 degrees in place.

```text
REPEAT 2 TIMES
{
   MOVE_FORWARD()
   ROTATE_LEFT()
}
```

Where does the robot end, and which way does it face?

options.why: Correct. Trace each move and turn in order.
The robot turns in every pass, including the last.
ROTATE_LEFT turns the robot counterclockwise.
The robot moves forward in each pass.

questions.stem: A network has computers P, Q, R, S, T, U. The direct connections are: P–R, Q–R, Q–S, Q–T, R–S, R–U. What is the minimum number of connections that must fail for computer U to be unable to communicate with computer S?

options.why: After that many failures a path still remains.
Correct. Removing 1 well-chosen connection separates U from S; removing fewer always leaves a path.
Some set of 1 connection already disconnects them.
Not every connection needs to fail.
